item.title: Agent-based modeling reveals how bats navigate dense group emergences
item.description: Bats face a complex navigation challenge when emerging from densely populated roosts, where vast numbers take off at once in dark, confined spaces. Each bat must avoid collisions with walls and conspecifics while locating the exit, all amidst overlapping acoustic signals. item.title: Sperm motility in mice with oligo-astheno-teratozoospermia restored by in vivo injection and electroporation of naked mRNA
item.description: Oligo-astheno-teratozoospermia (OAT), a recurrent cause of male infertility, is the most frequent disorder of spermatogenesis with a predominantly genetic origin. Patients and mice bearing mutations in the ARMC2 gene exhibit reduced sperm concentration, multiple morphological defects, and impaired motility, defining a canonical OAT phenotype. item.description: The brain is thought to optimise behaviour by generating predictions based on learned statistical regularities. item.title: Intracellular expression of a fluorogenic DNA aptamer using retron Eco2
item.description: DNA aptamers are short, single-stranded DNA molecules that bind specifically to a range of targets such as proteins, cells, and small molecules. Typically, they are utilized in the development of therapeutic agents, diagnostics, drug delivery systems, and biosensors. item.title: Toward neuroanatomical and cognitive foundations of macaque social tolerance grades
item.description: The macaque genus includes 25 species with diverse social systems, ranging from low to high social tolerance grades. Such interspecific behavioral variability provides a unique model to tackle the evolutionary foundation of primate social brain. Yet, the neuroanatomical correlates of these social tolerance grades remain unknown. item.description: Cells must adopt flexible regulatory strategies to make decisions regarding their fate, including differentiation, apoptosis, or survival in the face of various external stimuli. item.title: Acetylation of H3K115 is associated with fragile nucleosomes at CpG island promoters and active regulatory sites
item.description: Acetylation of lysine residues in the tail domain of histone H3 is well characterised, but lysine residues in the histone globular domain are also acetylated. item.title: Ancient photoreceptor shapes behavioural responses
item.description: Experiments on Drosophila show that an evolutionarily conserved photoreceptor that senses light outside of the retina can regulate responses to direct visual cues.
